scored.name: KneeWall Pivot Bracket
scored.moat_mechanism: DE utility model/EU registered design on locking pivot geometry; design-around easy, DE-only utility model
scored.reasoning: Real niche pain, installer channel from VELUX network, B2B pair about EUR 20 vs landed 7-10. Moat is a thin utility model; novelty unsearched, Amazon not checked. One-off purchase, no repeat. Capital fits.

scored.name: WoodSafe Clamp Carrier
scored.moat_mechanism: EU registered design on pad; no real moat, would need blind-maker licence
scored.reasoning: Retail 22-29 is below EUR 35 and tooling 3-4.5k is spent on a copyable part. Only viable as licence/B2B to blind makers, which is a long negotiation. Needs a signed buyer before tooling.

scored.name: Koppelhake Retrofit Clip
scored.moat_mechanism: Channel/framework deal with BRFs; no IP of substance
scored.reasoning: Niche Swedish B2B repair part; box 35-49 vs landed about 15-30 gives only 40-60% GM and retail hooks are cheap (unverified). Maintenance repeat plausible; tooling 2-3.5k for a small market. Test with a BRF before tooling.

scored.name: Roof-Window Rain-Hush Kit
scored.moat_mechanism: Independent acoustic test report (rivals pay same) plus material spec; commodity pads
scored.reasoning: Demand evidence is old UK forums; efficacy unvalidated and OEM warranty risk. Installer upsell is a credible low-CAC channel and price 39-59 absorbs CAC. Pre-test cheaply before spending lab fee.

scored.name: Wind-Rated Wall-Sleeve Flap
scored.moat_mechanism: DE utility model on spring-magnet closure plus test report; commodity category
scored.reasoning: Demand source is AI-flavoured forums, unverified. Fire-safety/ventilation certification risk, weak social channel, installer reach only partial. Price 29-39 borderline.

scored.name: Balcony-Door Gust Stop
scored.moat_mechanism: EU registered design plus possible DE utility model; crowded, easy design-around
scored.reasoning: Price 24-29 below EUR 35, tooling 3-4.5k, crowded with catches and baby locks, Amazon exposure. Housing-association bulk is the only angle.

scored.name: RoboSill flush ramp threshold profile
scored.moat_mechanism: EU registered design plus utility model on ramp+insert; spec-in via housing associations
scored.reasoning: Robot-friendly floor trend is real but Nordic threshold prevalence unverified; extruded profiles are copyable. B2B 20-28 vs landed 8-12 is about 2.3x, retail about 3.5x. Extrusion die is cheap; capital fits.

scored.name: Cabinet Bay robot dock insert
scored.moat_mechanism: EU registered design plus utility model on airflow/drip-tray layout; installer switching cost weak
scored.reasoning: Price 89-139 absorbs CAC and Bosch/Ecovacs validates the idea, but a joiner copies it in a week and dock models vary, forcing fit variants. Flat-pack freight keeps landed 28-42, GM about 55-65%. First order 4-6.5k acceptable.

scored.name: Lab-tested H13 filter + brush kits
scored.moat_mechanism: Independent lab report plus TM; rivals can pay same
scored.kill_reason: Robot-vacuum aftermarket consumables are dominated by private label/OEM kits (hard kill); first order up to 9.5k incl. test fees at the limit
scored.reasoning: Repeat revenue is attractive but marketplace is saturated and test report moat is small; many model SKUs needed. Killed on private-label rule.

scored.name: Robot-mower wash stand + pad refills
scored.moat_mechanism: EU registered design plus utility model; proprietary pad refill format
scored.reasoning: Robot-mower growth is real, price 79-99 absorbs CAC, but Mammotion already sells a stand and model-specific cradles multiply SKUs. Capital 4.5-7.5k plus 1.5-3.5k tooling is heavy for 10 h/week; seasonal.

scored.name: Dock-tank descaler tablets
scored.moat_mechanism: Contract-formulator exclusivity; easily reverse engineered
scored.reasoning: High GM and consumable repeat, but demand unverified, price 19-29, CLP/SDS burden, OEM warranty concerns, and paid CAC is high on a low-ticket item. Subscription LTV helps only if retention holds.

scored.name: Washable mop-pad system
scored.moat_mechanism: Registered design/TM only; OEM formats likely protected
scored.kill_reason: Compatible-pad category is private-label dominated and FTO risk; no real moat
scored.reasoning: Plutoos/JETtools and many marketplace sellers already serve it. Killed.

scored.name: Anti-tangle comb roller upgrade
scored.moat_mechanism: Utility model on comb insert; OEMs likely hold prior art, FTO required
scored.kill_reason: Aftermarket robot parts dominated by private label; FTO risk, first order 5-8k plus tooling 2.5-4.5k on unverified patent position
scored.reasoning: High risk of infringing OEM patents and multi-model fitment. Killed.

scored.name: Nordic FTX Filter Club
scored.moat_mechanism: ISO 16890 test report/optional RISE P-mark for installer and BRF sales, installer price list plus subscription, registered design on frame
scored.reasoning: Best of the set: OEM sets EUR 31-58 are seen so 35-49 pricing is anchored, annual replacement gives true repeat, and installers resell at near-zero CAC via founders' network. Moat is a certificate competitors can also buy, so about 3. OEMs claim only originals keep performance; test report cost unquoted. Low capital (1.5-3k + about 3.5k).

scored.name: BRF Ventilation Year-Pack
scored.moat_mechanism: Founder BRF relationships plus per-building size schedule embedded in maintenance plan; shared test report
scored.reasoning: B2B annual recurring orders with low CAC and a cheap pilot (1.8-2.8k). Margin about 3x at BRF price 22-28 vs 6-9. Moat is relationship and survey switching cost; BRF sales cycles and valve-fit variety are the risk, and the relationships are assumed.

scored.name: Window Seal Service Kit
scored.moat_mechanism: Own formulation spec plus applicator design plus installer/BRF citation in service docs
scored.reasoning: Annual care documented by window makers; silicone spray is the cheap incumbent so willingness to pay 24-29 is unproven. Ex-VELUX installer channel is credible; CLP check needed. Low capital.

scored.name: Heat-Pump Pollen Insert Refills
scored.moat_mechanism: Installer relationships and fit database; no IP
scored.reasoning: Many model families, no price evidence, installer demand unconfirmed and founders' HVAC channel is not their stated edge. Repeat is fine but the fit database is the only barrier.

scored.name: Homecare Move-In Box
scored.moat_mechanism: Bundle of certified SKUs plus B2B gifting contracts; unverified agent demand
scored.reasoning: Depends on N014/N016 working first; gifting demand is pure assumption. Bundle GM about 60%. Treat as phase 2.

scored.name: Hood Filter Pack
scored.moat_mechanism: None beyond fit database
scored.reasoning: No moat, price 25-35 below preference, OEM and private-label spares compete; the founders have no hood channel. Cheap to try but weak.

scored.name: KeyPouch amenity dispenser + keyed refill pouch
scored.moat_mechanism: Consumable lock-in via own keyed pouch fitment, EU registered design, Danish utility model; Meadow and locking dispensers exist
scored.reasoning: Only idea with a true razor/blade mechanism and a regulatory tailwind (PPWR hospitality mini-ban), though dates conflict (2026 vs 2030) and Nordic small-operator demand is unverified; hospitality relationships are unproven. Pouch recurring at EUR 8-12 vs about 1 empty gives high margin; filled cosmetics adds compliance, so sell empty/partner-filled pouches first. Tooling 3.5-4.5k is within cap but near it (get 3 quotes) and total capital about 9-10k is the stretch. Copyable in 6-12 months.

scored.name: Fire-tested clip-on bunk privacy pod
scored.moat_mechanism: Flame test certificate on assembly plus registered design; certified fabric is purchasable
scored.reasoning: B2B per-bed price 49-65 vs landed 18-26 (about 2.5-3x). Swedish/Danish fire rules unverified and no repeat; small hostel buyer pool. Moat modest.

scored.name: Kommun-matched kitchen sorting station
scored.moat_mechanism: Per-municipality label/fraction dataset plus registered design; generic rack easy to copy
scored.reasoning: Regulatory driver date uncertain (deferral reported) and no in-apartment requirement verified. B2B bulk 29-39 vs 11-15 landed is about 2.6x. Long BRF cycles for a 10 h/week team; no repeat.

scored.name: Roof-window corner re-seal patch kit
scored.moat_mechanism: Die-cut geometry per window family, design registration; mild know-how barrier
scored.reasoning: Forum leaks show pain but competing flashing tapes not checked. Price 34-45, cheap die, ex-VELUX knowledge helps but conflict/confidentiality and warranty-claim risk. Fair margin, no repeat.

scored.name: Hospitality bed-leg bug interceptors
scored.moat_mechanism: Registered design only; existing interceptors already do the function
scored.reasoning: High margin but no moat, marketplace already served, tooling 3-4.5k near cap, no hospitality relationships stated. Not a durable asset.

scored.name: KeyPouch Breakfast portion dispenser
scored.moat_mechanism: Shared keyed pouch fitment, registered design; portion dispensers common
scored.reasoning: Phase 2 of N020; food-contact compliance, unclear legal scope for B&Bs, many portion dispensers exist. Only worth it after the amenity line proves the fitment.
